Violation ID: 8251179

Unconventional: No

Inspection Date: 10/03/2025
Comments: On October 3 2025, the Department conducted a follow up inspection in response to IR 3265061 of the OGM 1 OG Well.The findings were as follows:At the time of inspection, an Act 9 sign was installed at the access road. The access road appeared stable with no observed accelerated erosion or sedimentation concerns. The well appeared equipped for production. No fluid leaks are observed around the well head and associated equipment. A well tag was present with all required information. The GPU appeared to be in sound condition with no fluid leaks or discharges observed.In the Department's previous inspection on 5/15/2025 (IR 3979004), elevated conductivity readings were obtained in an area of a suspected release near the production tank. Upon inspection of this area during today's inspection, a roll of dumpster from McCutcheon Enterprises was on site and appeared to be full. There appeared to be fresh gravel in the location of previously elevated conductivity readings/suspected release area.The Department obtained conductivity readings in similar locations of the previously elevated readings and obtained readings of 0.05mS, 0.09mS, and 0.07mS. These readings were comparable/lower than the background conductivity reading of 0.14mS.The Department received a response from the operator on 5/29/2025 stating: "We will inspect site and check soil for possible need of removal". The Department has not received any further communication regarding remediation of the release.The operator is requested to submit a written response within seven (7) days of the receipt of this report. This written response should include an incident report, a timeline of remedial measures, and plan for/or how remediation of the release was conducted. The Department is requesting how the operator quantified the amount spilled. The Department also requests the waste manifest from the site remediation be submitted upon receipt.Based on today's inspection violations under IR 3265061 will remain outstanding for the release pending receipt and review of the requested information.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: EQT ARO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 6/06/2024
Violation Code: 78a66(b)1 - REPORTING AND REMEDIATING SPILLS AND RELEASES – Reporting releases – Operator or other responsible party failed to report spills and releases of regulated substances to the Department.
Violation ID: 8190156
Permit API: 081-21946
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Plunketts Creek Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 6/06/2024
Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to a notification from the operator of the discovery of a release of an estimated 20 gallons of a mixture of produced fluid and fresh water. According to the notification, fluid with electrical conductivity (EC) of 10-13 mS/cm was discovered on the pad surface in an area southeast of the well heads when secondary containment was removed from the pad surface. The notification also stated that a shallow trench has been dug along the southeast edge of the secondary containment to collect any additional fluid with elevated EC that may leach out from beneath the containment. The area impacted by the release was estimated to be 30 ft by 50 ft. I met with company man Steven Spitler upon arriving on location. It rained heavily during this inspection. Report Details

Violation ID: 972776
Permit API: 129-29003
Unconventional: Yes
County: Westmoreland

Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 10/13/2022
Comments: On October 13, 2022, the Department conducted a Routine inspection at the Sinay well pad in Sewickley Township, Westmoreland County. Present were myself, ET Marcella Dantzler, those listed from the SWDO OG Team, and EQT representatives Joe Eversman and Logan Dominick.The following was observed:The Act 9 sign was at the entrance of the access road, and was not obstructed by vegetation (see photo 2). The ER and PPC plans were not available immediately upon arrival (see photo 3). A site safety and environmental plan was found in the office onsite. A PPC plan was also in the office, but missing required components. Neither the secondary containment inspection records nor the well permit were available onsite when requested. A sediment basin was observed along the left side of the access road, looking towards the pad. A forebay cleanout was observed on the opposite side, with a culvert connecting them under the access road (see photo 5). Cattails were observed in the sediment basin. A further review will be conducted to ensure that they are part of the PCSM plan. A soil stockpile was observed along the left side of the access road, immediately before entering the pad (see photo 6). The operator was actively drilling onsite. This is the first well being drilled. The operator intends to drill 4 wells total. A destabilized area of soil was discovered behind the sound wall on the eastern side of the well pad (see photo 15). Preexisting metal and brick was observed outside of the LOD at this location, as was noted in the site E and S plans (see photo 16). A tear in the rig site containment was observed at the southern side of the pad. This was brought to Mr. Eversman's attention, who immediately called in a crew to repair it (see photo 12). Tanks and containers onsite that contained regulated substances were labelled, showed no evidence of leaks/discharges (see photos 13 and 14). The production tanks were within secondary containment (see photo 17). A puddle was observed at the northeastern corner of the containment. A soil conductivity reading was taken in this puddle, which read 200 Micro Siemens. The rig site containment appeared to be nearly full at its northeastern corner. A soil conductivity reading was taken at this corner, which read 390 Micro Siemens. The Department inquired with Mr. Eversman about whether the containment is pumped regularly. Mr. Eversman stated that the site containment gets pumped multiple times daily as needed. A pump truck later came to pump the containment during this inspection. A sediment-laden discharge to WOTC was discovered upon returning to the access road entrance (see photo 23). This discharge was flowing into a sewer drain that emptied into a field across the road from the well pad, through a culvert (see photo 21). This culvert was found to be approximately 80% full with sediment (see photo 22). Near the end of the inspection, EQT representative Logan Dominick arrived to the site, who was informed of the Department's findings. Mr. Dominick was able to provide an electronic copy of the PPC plan onsite, this was requested to be emailed to the Department for further review. He also stated to the Department that CFS and a silt pad will be installed around and over the sewer grate to prevent further discharge to the WOTC. He also stated that the site ERP and PPC plans had previously been placed into the mailboxes attached to the Act 9 sign, and that they were likely removed by a nuisance third party.Based on observations from this inspection, the Department recommends that the aforementioned unstable soil spot behind the sound wall is re-stabilized. Violations are being issued for discharging to the waters of the commonwealth, failing to have an adequate ER AND PPC plan onsite, failing to have the drill permit onsite, and failing to have secondary containment inspection records onsite.

Comments: On January 6, 2022, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted an administrative inspection for a spill at the Inflection Energy Hensler Well Pad. On January 5, 2022, around 2140, Zac Subra reported a spill of approximately 30 gallons of hydraulic fluid to the well pad surface. At about 920 on January 6, 2022, DEP spoke with Zac Subra on the phone. Mr. Subra said a hydraulic fluid line on a water truck ruptured and caused the spill. Inflection contractors began removing the hydraulic fluid and excavating the impacted soil immediately. Inflection contractors excavated an area of about 20 ft. X 15 ft. of the pad surface. Due to the ground being frozen, Inflection contractors only had to scrape the top of the pad surface to remove the impacted soil in the previously noted area. The impacted soil was added to a rolloff dumpster and hauled to a landfill. Inflection then went back to the pad during the day to verify that the impacted soil had been completely removed. Zac said a small amount of remaining soil had to be removed at this time since it was not observed earlier in the morning. The small amount of soil was added to barrels and is awaiting approval to be disposed of. Inflection then backfilled the excavated area with clean fill. Photos of the area excavated and clean up were provided by Inflection Energy. The spill of hydraulic fluid outside of containment is a violation of Clean Streams Law Section 402(b), Solid Waste Management Act Section 301, and Chapter 78a.54. The violations have been immediately corrected.

Report Details

Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 8259072
Permit API: 117-22308
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Tioga Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 12/16/2025
Comments: Site inspection conducted to review drill cuttings processing activity and secondary containment conditions. Meeting on site today with JKLM Drilling Supervisor Ron Burdick. Site inspection conducted with JKLM HSE Field Supervisor Terra Tokarz. Weather conditions at time of inspection are sunny and 24F.According to Mr. Burdick, the Highlands #14 tophole rig is on location to batch drill the surface and intermediate strings for six Marcellus wells. The Highlands #14 rigged up on 12/10/25. The rig is currently drilling the 4HM well (API #117-22308) at a depth of 750'. The surface casing will be set at a depth of 800-820'. Casing run and cementing is expected later this evening. The surface casing is being drilled on air/mist and there are no chemicals added to facilitate cuttings processing. This is the second well to have the surface casing drilled. A Patterson rig is scheduled to return to the site to drill tangents and laterals. This is a new well pad and there are no producing wells or production equipment on location. R and R Oilfield Services is conducting solids control in the rig backyard. An excavator is mixing drill cuttings with wood fiber for solidification. A crew is manually clearing drill cuttings from rig shakers adjacent to the centrifuge deck. Cuttings will be loaded out by dump truck and hauled to the Waste Management Phoenix Resources landfill. Gas Field Specialists water trucks are observed on site unloading water. JKLM submitted a Request Alternate Waste Management Practices (OG71-A) application for the Belz 2001 Pad on 10/21/25. The Department approved the request on 10/22/25. The intent of the authorization for onsite drill cuttings processing is to remove the solid fraction from the liquid (drilling muds and fluids) so that drilling fluid can be reused. For more information, refer to the Belz OG-71 Form A application for drill cuttings processing (eFACTS Authorization #1546423).During this inspection puddled fluid on site was screened using an Oakton PCTS 50 water conductivity meter and a Hanna Groline soil conductivity meter. While screening puddles around the containment perimeter near the freshwater cement tanks, the Department observed fluid with elevated electrical conductivity (photos 8-11). Screenings with conductivity reading 'Over Range' (>19.99 mS/cm) were noted and a water sample was taken based on the elevated reading. Sample 4406-020 collected at 11:48 from fluid puddled on pad rock surface between tank rig secondary containment structure and freshwater cement tanks. Ms. Tokarz indicated that JKLM personnel would also collect a sample and vacuum water from the area. Violation noted for potential pollution. Additional violations may be issued pending results of water sample analysis.

Unconventional: No
County: McKean

Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 1/03/2024
Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to reported concerns at the tank battery located near this well.This conventional well is equipped with a pump jack, the well's API number is displayed on the jack. A tank battery consisting of a 210 bbl stock tank and a plastic brine tank within an earthen containment is located beside the well. There is evidence of heavy deer activity inside and outside of the containment in the vicinity of the brine tank. Specific conductance (SPC) of the fluid inside of the containment is near 1000 uS/cm and the SPC of the soil on the exterior of the containment berm is also elevated (~800 uS/cm). This indicates that the fluid released inside the containment has seeped through the containment wall. Water in the ditch just outside of the containment also has elevated SPC (~ 1300 uS/cm). The elevated SPC readings were detected in an approximate 3' x 10' section of the ditch that also has signs of heavy deer activity. There is no apparent impact to the ditch beyond where the deer tracks are present, as SPC concentrations of the water quickly return to background levels.There is currently a minimal amount of fluid in the brine tank, there are no structural issues apparent with the tank or plumbing. I contacted TJ Allshouse and he agreed to an upcoming field meeting to further investigate the matter.Upon discovering the source, amount and extent of the releases at this tank battery, appropriate remediation options will be explored and documented in upcoming inspections. The inability for the tank battery to contain fluid inside of it will also need to be addressed for compliance to be achieved.

Comments: On 03/26/2024, a follow up inspection was conducted at the Fowler Well Site following routine complete inspections that were conducted for each well on 01/03/2024 (See IR 3670374 for example). I was accompanied by Environmental Trainee Olivia Holley (PA DEP). It was noted that sediment was being transported towards the main township road, Little Daniel's Run Road, down the side of the road to a storm grate. Sediment was accumulating within the rock lined channel and pooling at the base of the channel, adjacent to the access road.It was discussed with EQT via phone for plans to install a rubber belting water bar to divert the spring water towards the rock lined channel instead of flowing down the center of the access road. EQT also used dust suppressant on the road. The following was observed during inspection on 03/26/2024:The rubber belting water bar was not yet installed on the access road. The access road displayed some dust suppressant, however I recommend that additional is applied, focusing on the beginning of the access road where the spring is out letting and the water is leaving the site. There was a section of dust suppressant at the top of the road near the tanks, however it was unclear if this area was existing (Photos 1-6).Newly installed storm grate at the base of the rock lined channel was in generally good condition. Some sediment accumulation noted on the bottom. No sediment noted within stone around the storm grate coming from the stabilized bank or the channel (Photos 7, 8).Sediment was accumulating along the base of the access road and main township road which appeared to be originating from the site. This sediment was leading towards the storm grate along the main township road. Sediment did not appear to be accumulating within the storm grate (Photos 9-12).Sediment laden water leaving the access road was noted leading towards the township storm grate. Some rills were noted within the sediment (Photos 13-18).The channel on the property across the street where the township storm grate and culvert outlets did not appear to be accumulating sediment from the access road (Photo 19). Overview of access road, storm grates and outlet across the street leading to Little Daniels Run (Photo 20).Due to the continuing discharge of sediment laden water off of the access road and sediment accumulation of sediment along the main township road, violations of 102.4(b)1, 102.11(a), and 78a.53 are being issued.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 3/03/2025 to REPSOL OIL & GAS USA LLC in Covington Township, Tioga county. 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: REPSOL OIL & GAS USA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/03/2025
Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 8223192
Permit API: 117-22227
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Covington Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/03/2025
Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to a notification from the operator that a fluid was released from secondary containment on the well pad and it flowed off of the well pad. Upon arriving on location I met with Repsol representative Roy Trimmer. He showed me where the fluid peaked out of the containment, down the pad side slope, and along a vegetated infiltration berm. The secondary containment is present along the west side of the well pad. The secondary containment had previously held a battery of upright tanks containing produced fluid. The tanks have been removed from the location and a crew was working to remove the secondary containment during this inspection. The leak in the containment occurred along the west side of the containment near the southwest corner of the pad. The fluid ran down the west pad side slope near the southwest corner of the pad and along a vegetated, earthen infiltration berm. The fluid ran along the toe of the berm. The berm ends at an infiltration basin. The soil was moist along the path of the fluid. The fluid appeared to stop at the rock-lined entrance to the basin. Fluid present in the infiltration basin near the area of the leak along the west side of the containment had electrical conductivity (EC) readings between 1392 uS/cm to 1500 uS/cm as measured by the Oakton water EC meter. The EC readings in the soil on the Hanna soil EC meter were 2070 uS/cm at the highest not far from the toe of the pad side slope to 250 uS/cm where the path of the fluid ended at the entrance to the infiltration basin. Repsol representative Andrew Senefelder arrived on location during this inspection. He told me that their consultant Resource Environmental would be taking soil samples from the path of the fluid as well as a water sample from inside the secondary containment. He said that due to the EC readings in the soil, they did not anticipate finding any exceedances in the soil; however, as a precaution, Repsol plans to scrape the soil along the flow path of the fluid release anyway, he stated.Mr. Senefelder then left and I took sample 0718-253 from the fluid within the secondary containment near where the leak occurred near the southwest corner of the well pad. The sample was sent to the state laboratory the next day to be analyzed for SAC 942 plus Al, Sr, and Br.Due to the unknown spill volume, the Department recommends pursuing Act 2 remediation. In a phone call with PA DEP Water Quality Specialist Supervisor Sean VanFleet on 3/3/25 at 1600, Repsol representative Kris Perritt committed to pursuing Act 2 remediation for this release. Violations noted.

Report Details

Violation Code: SWMA 610(1) - UNLAWFUL CONDUCT - Person dumped or deposited, or permitted the dumping or depositing, of solid waste onto the surface of the ground or underground or into the waters of the Commonwealth, without a permit for the dumping of such solid wastes from DEP.
Violation ID: 921741
Permit API: 085-23523
Unconventional: No
County: Mercer
Municipality: West Salem Twp
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 6/24/2021
Comments: Stopped to inspect this gas well a day after the reported spill incident as the result of a piece of farm equipment had that had hit this gas well causing a release of gas and production fluids. The incident happened at approximately 11 AM on June 23, 2021. I was notified the same day by phone at 1 PM by Matt Kleese from Diamond Energy. The summary of the situation is as follows: the gas well was hit by a piece of equipment being operated by Centerra Co-op for the farmer. The tubing on the gas well was completely sheared off by this piece of equipment. Nobody was injured. The gas well had an approximate pressure of 680 psi and vented for approximately 1 minute after the incident before it just basically stopped. Centerra is taking full responsibility and is handling the clean-up. The gas well was presently shut in with a new piece of tubing in place. The operator reported less than one barrel of oil that was released from this well. It was difficult to say how much oil was released from a spill like this where the production fluids are spread over the land area by the venting (blowing) gas. There was a 60 yard x 35 yard area around the well where the oil mist had been scraped off the ground surface. No residual of any kind was seen. There was however an oil residual on the leaves of the trees for an approximate 80 yard stretch. I contacted Jason Nowakowski from Centerra regarding the clean-up and the ownership of the trees on the field edge. He said they have hauled the soil back to their shop for proper disposal. He also said that he would have to get back to me on the ownership of the trees.

Permit API: 123-49194
Unconventional: No

Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/14/2026
Comments: This inspection was conducted to evaluate the status of violations issued on 9/18/2025 and 4/17/2026 associated with the construction of the well site for this proposed conventional well and the access road leading to it. Since the 4/17/2026 inspection, Trinity Mineral Partners (TMP) submitted multiple versions of an updated E and S plan that included additional BMPs and methods to stabilize all disturbed areas. At the time of this inspection, the latest version of the updated E and S plan has not yet met the expectations of the Department's Technical Services staff, as was indicated in a 5/11/2026 email to William Cenk.Throughout this inspection, we observed that a majority of the practices prescribed in the latest version of the updated E and S plan have been implemented. Inlet/outlet rock protection was placed at the installed culverts, rock filters placed in the roadside ditch in the vicinity of the well site for proposed Well # 3, and a combination of erosion blankets and mulch was applied to temporarily stabilize most of the disturbed areas. TMP indicated that seed was applied prior to mulching/placement of the erosion blanket. Erosion blanket was missing upslope of Culvert 1 and there was no evidence of hydro-seeding. The placement of grubbing material along the southern side of the access road that has displaced stream flow continues to result in accelerated erosion and washout along the southern edge of the road and perimeter of the well site for proposed Well # 4.The Department suggests the removal of the stockpile material from approximately the outlet location of Culvert 3 westerly to the newly established point of concentrated flow. Currently, it appears the streamflow is obstructed and migrated towards the pad/access road creating concentrated flow which cannot be stabilized. Without proper stabilization, the additional flow due to the construction activity appears to be causing accelerated erosion and sedimentation to Wetland G. The removal of the waste areas would potentially allow the flow to migrate back to its original drainage path and allow for successful installation of temporary stabilization BMPs, per plan. Department staff can be available for consultation/direction during the removal operation. Waste areas are not to be discarded in other floodways or wetlands. After the submission of the updated and complete E and S plan to Brian Ayers (brayers@pa.gov), temporary stabilization shall be finished. A follow up inspection will be conducted following the completion of the temporary stabilization. A preapplication meeting must be submitted/scheduled before June 15, 2026 in order to address any outstanding violations.Violations that were cited in the 9/18/2025 and 4/17/2026 inspection reports remain unaddressed.The following were in attendance for this inspection:DEP - Aquatic Biologist Samantha Lutz, Aquatic Biologist Jessica McDuff and WQSS Brian Ayers.Trinity Mineral Partners - Kyle Miller, Brian Bennett and Todd Fantaskey (Northwest Soil Services)

Comments: This Admin inspection is to document the voicemail (received on 10/29/2025) and subsequent phone conversation (had on 10/30/2025) the Department had with K Petroleum Inc representative Robert Inghram regarding the Mclvaine 1 well site located in Somerset Township, Washington County.Mr. Inghram's voicemail stated that on 10/29/2025 a well tender at the Mclvaine well site discovered a 7-10 gal release from the production tank on site onto the ground within tanks earthen dike. Mr. Inghram stated clean up was started promptly.During the subsequent phone conversation, Mr. Inghram reiterated that a 7-10 gallon release occurred at the Mclvaine well site on 10/29/2025 and that upon its discovery, absorbent pads and peatsorb were promptly put down in the release area to contain the release and that once the absorbents are removed, any contaminated material along with the pads will be properly disposed of and the tank will be cleaned off.The Department inquired what the substance was and at what time this incident occurred/was discovered. Mr. Inghram stated that he did not have that information but would provide it to the Department upon its receipt. The Department verbally requested Mr. Inghram provide the Department with any photos taken when the incident was discovered as well as after clean up was conducted, provide the Department with a timeline of events, and provide the Department with a waste manifest for the disposed contaminated materials upon its receipt. Mr. Inghram stated he would provide the aforementioned information in an email to the Department.The Department also inquired whether Mr. Inghram contacted the Department's Southwest Regional Office or the 24Hr Emergency Spill Hotline to report this release. Mr. Inghram stated that he was not aware of either of these numbers or requirements, therefore did not contact either one. The Department provided Mr. Inghram with both numbers and recommended he report any future spills, releases, or incidents to either of those numbers in accordance with 78.66(a). Based on the voicemail and phone conversation, violations associated with 78.66a are being noted and immediately corrected, however, future violations may be forthcoming for the release dependent upon the Department's findings during a subsequent site inspection.
